title: Stream Analytics: windows, watermarks and late-arriving data

videos.script: Quitanda wants one number on a screen. How many checkouts in the last minute. {{screen}} It sounds like counting. It is not, because the clicks do not arrive in the order they happened. {{order}} A phone loses signal in a tunnel. It keeps its clicks and sends them a minute later, all at once. {{tunnel}} So which minute does a late click belong to? The one in which the customer tapped, or the one in which Azure heard about it? {{minute}} Stream Analytics answers with event time, a timestamp the app writes into each click. It counts in windows, and there are five kinds. {{windows}} A window cannot wait for ever. The service keeps a watermark, a line saying that anything older is late. {{watermark}} Late events are dropped or adjusted, and you choose which. There is no emulator for Stream Analytics. So you will run the same idea in a short Python program of the course's own, against the Event Hubs emulator. {{program}} Then you will see the bill, which runs every hour the job is on. {{bill}}
